sections.overview: Nomada atroscutellaris is a European cuckoo bee recorded as a cleptoparasite of the mining bee Andrena viridescens.
sections.identification: Species-level identification in the diverse genus Nomada depends on diagnostic structures; colour or a common name alone is not a safe guide.
sections.habitat: The host A. viridescens nests in sparsely vegetated banks and grasslands where speedwells grow; parasite records near host nesting sites suggest it shares these habitats.
sections.diet: As a Nomada cleptoparasite, its larva uses a host nest and provisions rather than a pollen store gathered by the female.
sections.behavior: Its known host association is narrower than host use across Nomada as a whole; compare N. argentata, tied to another Andrena species.
sections.reproduction: The host record points to A. viridescens nests, but the sources do not detail the parasite’s oviposition sequence or development period.
sections.ecology: Because A. viridescens relies on speedwell pollen and open nesting ground, protecting only flowers or only bare soil may not preserve the host-parasite relationship.
sections.conservation: The European Red List classifies N. atroscutellaris as Least Concern at European and EU scales; local scarcity can still occur where its host is rare.
